item.title: GAČR grant supports DBGI research in Prague
item.description: The Czech Science Foundation (GAČR) has awarded Tito Damiani a Standard Project grant for “Metabolomics-driven discovery of plant chemical novelty and its insecticidal potential” (Project No. 26-21882S). Providing approximately €300,000 from 1 January 2026 to 31 December 2028, the project is based in the Pluskal Lab at IOCB Prague.

item.title: Three weeks at Kew: more than 600 samples for DBGI
item.description: From 22 September to 10 October 2025, Kateřina Kučerová and Tito Damiani from IOCB Prague, Mazzarine Laboureau from the University of Neuchâtel, and Davide Rovelli from the University of Parma travelled to London to conduct a sampling campaign at Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, home to one of the world’s most diverse living plant collections.

item.title: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew joins the DBGI network
item.description: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew has formally joined the DBGI network, extending the initiative beyond continental Europe and bringing one of the world’s leading botanical institutions into the collaboration. The partnership began on 22 September 2025 with a DBGI sampling campaign across Kew’s living collections. Read about the three-week Kew sampling campaign.

item.title: Flore-Alpe, Champex-Lac joins the DBGI network
item.description:
Flore-Alpe, the alpine botanical garden at Champex-Lac, has joined the DBGI network, adding the initiative’s first botanical collection dedicated specifically to alpine plants.

Situated at approximately 1,500 metres in the Valais Alps, Flore-Alpe maintains more than 4,000 plant species from the local flora and mountain regions around the world. Its concentrated alpine collection gives DBGI access to plants adapted to a wide range of high-elevation environments and complements the network’s lower-altitude gardens.

item.title: SNSF Weave grant supports MetaboLinkAI
item.description: The Swiss National Science Foundation has awarded MetaboLinkAI (Grant 10002786) a Weave/Lead Agency grant. Beginning on 1 April 2025, the project will run until 31 March 2029. The SNSF record lists eleven applicants from institutions in Switzerland and France, with ETH Zurich named as the Swiss research institution.

item.title: Prague Botanical Garden joins the DBGI network
item.description: Prague Botanical Garden has formally joined the DBGI network as its first partner garden in Czechia. Situated across approximately 25 hectares in Prague, the garden maintains around 15,000 cultivated plant species in its outdoor collections and greenhouses, including the Fata Morgana tropical greenhouse.

item.title: SNSF R'EQUIP grant strengthens mass spectrometry infrastructure in Fribourg
item.description: The Swiss National Science Foundation has awarded the University of Fribourg an R’EQUIP infrastructure grant for “Biological complexity addressed by mass spectrometry” (Grant 229588). Beginning on 1 December 2024, the CHF 700,000 project will run until 30 November 2025.

item.title: SNSF grant supports "Anticipating the Chemistry of Life"
item.description: The Swiss National Science Foundation has awarded “Anticipating the Chemistry of Life” (Grant 10000895) to Pierre-Marie Allard at the University of Fribourg. Beginning on 1 October 2024, the CHF 397,854 project will run until 30 September 2028.

item.title: Botanical Garden of the University of Fribourg joins the DBGI network
item.description: The Botanical Garden of the University of Fribourg has formally joined the DBGI network, building on its role in the initiative’s earliest pilot phase. It provided one of the first living collections in which DBGI’s sampling, documentation and traceability workflows could be developed in practice.

item.title: Postdoctoral researcher position - computational ecology, metabolomics and knowledge management for biodiversity research.
item.description: The Computational Ecology Group at the University of Neuchâtel, Switzerland, is offering a postdoctoral research position ! This postdoctoral project will be carried out in close collaboration with the COMMONS Lab in the Department of Biology at the University of Fribourg, Switzerland. This project is framed within the Digital Botanical Gardens Initiative (DBGI) and the wider Earth Metabolome Initiative (EMI), which aim to document the chemical diversity of living systems using untargeted metabolomic data and semantic web technologies. The candidate will integrate ecological data into this framework and explore the potential of this approach to characterize biodiversity in the landscape.

item.title: Botanical Garden of Neuchâtel joins the DBGI network
item.description:
The Botanical Garden of Neuchâtel has joined the DBGI network, formalising a long-standing collaboration with the Plant Eco-Metabolomics Group at the University of Neuchâtel.

The garden maintains eight botanical spaces, ranging from an evolution garden and medicinal-plant collections to an alpinum and greenhouses. This variety brings plants from contrasting taxonomic and environmental contexts within reach of a coordinated sampling campaign.

item.title: Postdoctoral researcher position: Knowledge Management in the Digital Botanical Gardens Initiative
item.description: A postdoctoral researcher position is available at the COMMONS Lab in the Department of Biology at the University of Fribourg , Switzerland. The candidate will develop and implement computational solutions to establish and manage a Knowledge Graph documenting the chemodiversity of living systems using both untargeted metabolomics data and semantic web technologies.

item.title: PhD position in eco-metabolomics: Investigating the ecological and evolutionary drivers of phytochemical diversity
item.description: The Computational Ecology Group at the Institute of Biology, University of Neuchâtel, is seeking a PhD student to investigate the ecological and evolutionary drivers of phytochemical diversity by leveraging the living collection in Swiss botanical gardens.

item.title: SNSF MetaDiv grant supports research on plant chemical diversity
item.description: The Swiss National Science Foundation has awarded MetaDiv: Ecological and Evolutionary Drivers of Phytochemical Diversity (Grant 215724) to Emmanuel Defossez at the University of Neuchâtel. The CHF 381,293 project will run from 1 July 2023 to 30 June 2027.

item.title: Seminar in the Botanical Garden of Zurich.
item.description: We will present both the DBGI and EMI at the Department of Systematic and Evolutionary Botany in Zurich (16:00 Monday 06 March 2023)

item.title: First DBGI-KM meeting !
item.description: We had our first official DBGI-KM meeting this Wednesday 22nd February 2023 !

item.title: swissuniversities Open Research Data grant awarded for the Swiss DBGI-KM
item.description: We are thrilled that our proposal “Knowledge Management in the Swiss Digital Botanical Gardens Initiative (Swiss DBGI-KM)” will be supported by a swissuniversities Open Research Data grant obtained for the Track B “Establish projects” call.
